subject: Rapid scale commitments & next steps
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Glover <alex.glover@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: rapid scale / streaming SLOs from today's call

Alex — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and a proposed set of commitments so we can align engineering + procurement on next steps. I captured the items we talked through and a suggested plan for the performance qualification run.

Key ask from NimbleHealth (as I understand it):
- Streaming inference with partial-token streaming to UI; 99th pct tail latency per token should be <= 200ms for interactive sessions.
- Sustained baseline throughput: ~400 concurrent streams during business hours.
- Short bursts: up to ~2,000 concurrent streams for ~60-120s during appointment-release events.
- Failover: if primary model variant saturates, fall back to a lower-cost quantized variant with identical API surface.

Our proposed commitments (subject to test results):
1) Warm pool: prewarmed pool sized to cover 25% of expected burst concurrency (we propose 500 prewarmed streams as a starting point).
2) Scale-up SLT: ramp additional capacity to 90% of requested burst capacity within 45s from first spike detection (targets measurable in canary).
3) Soft queuing: allow short request queueing (max 3s) during transition windows to preserve 99p latency SLA; queue behavior surfaced in logs and trace.
4) Canary tests: a 2-hour simulated release test using your workload (we'll need your sample traces/harness).

Next steps I propose:
- You to share a representative workload sample (request rate + sample payloads) — see attachment stub nimble-workload-sample.tar.gz.
- We provide an SLO matrix (attached as slo_matrix_v1.xlsx) and a warm-pool topology diagram.
- Schedule a 2-hour canary on our dedicated staging cluster (suggestion: Mon 2026-07-06 09:00 PT).
- Contractual: we can offer a 30-day prewarm credit if you commit to a Dedicated trial.

If that aligns, I'll schedule the canary and loop in our ops lead to define telemetry and debugging hooks.

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
From: Alex Glover <alex.glover@nimblehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Patel <jordan@nimblehealth.com>, ops@nimblehealth.com
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 18:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: rapid scale / streaming SLOs from today's call

Rishi — thanks for the crisp recap. Confirming a few items from our side and adding clarifications:

- 99p <= 200ms per-token goal is what Product needs for the live chat UI. If you can hit 150ms that's ideal, but 200ms is the absolute must-have.
- Bursts hit ~2k concurrency but only last 90s on average. They are tightly correlated with appointment window openings (we can provide timestamps).
- We use token-level streaming; partial responses must start showing within 120ms ideally so UI feels snappy.
- Audit requirement: we need 7-day retention of request/response traces for a small sample set and access to token-level latency histograms.

We'll attach a small sample harness and a short trace file this afternoon (ops@nimblehealth will send). For the fallback model, we need to understand the accuracy delta — can you provide a brief comparison during the canary?

Mon 2026-07-06 09:00 PT is fine for the canary window. We prefer the canary run to include a ramp from baseline -> burst -> relaxation so we can see scale-up and scale-down behavior.

Thanks,
Alex
Director, Platform Engineering | NimbleHealth
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Glover <alex.glover@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 09:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: rapid scale / streaming SLOs from today's call

Alex — perfect, thanks for the clarifications. Attached is the SLO matrix we've drafted for the canary (slo_matrix_v1.xlsx) and a topology sketch for the warm pool. Inline summary of the test plan and acceptance gates:

Acceptance gates (pass/fail):
- Latency: 99p per-token <= 200ms for the entire canary window (we'll report per-10s sliding windows).
- Streaming lead: median time-to-first-byte <= 120ms across sampled sessions.
- Availability: >= 99.9% successful stream establishments (no 5xx).
- Scale-up time: additional capacity to handle target concurrency increase within 45s for >= 90% of observed spike events.
- Queueing behavior: queued requests observe <= 3s median queue wait; we'll surface queue time in traces.

Test plan:
- Phase 1 (30m): baseline validation at 400 concurrent streams.
- Phase 2 (40m): controlled ramp to 2k concurrency over 60s; hold for 90s; observe scale-up and queueing.
- Phase 3 (30m): step-down and steady-state observations.

Data we'll need from Nimble: workload harness, representative payloads, and an example of your peak-event schedule. Please upload to the shared drive link I pasted earlier. We'll place link to perf logs and Grafana snapshots in Drive after the run.

Regarding fallback accuracy: our Research team will run the fallback (8-bit quantized) model against your eval prompts and provide a quick delta report — expecting 2-4% BLEU/ROUGE-like delta depending on prompt type; we'll share numbers prior to the canary.

I'll schedule the canary and send a calendar invite once we get the harness. Also including the attachment stubs: warmpool_topology.png and slo_matrix_v1.xlsx.

Best,
Rishi
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: NimbleHealth canary — pricing + prewarm credit suggestion

Lauren / Marissa — internal note on the Nimble canary: they are price-sensitive and want a short Dedicated trial to prove economics. Proposed commercial levers:

1) Offer a 30-day prewarm credit (covers warm pool sizing up to 500 streams) to remove friction for the initial test.
2) Include a one-time operational support day (SRE shadowing) during the canary at no charge.
3) If canary passes acceptance gates, propose a 6-month reserved commit with a right-sized warm pool and a 15% volume discount in month 1-3.

Operational ask for Marissa: please confirm whether a 500-stream warm pool is feasible on our staging Dedicated cluster on 2026-07-06 and estimate the infra cost for the credit proposal.
Operational ask for Lauren: if we give the prewarm credit, what is the lowest acceptable MSP margin for this deal (we need to preserve >45% gross margin).

I'll hold off final pricing with Alex until we confirm these two points.

Thanks,
Rishi
